I'd like to consider adding CLZ to Fusaka

https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7939

CLZ isn't CFI'd but if we want to send signal we are listening to dev community, would be a good one? (Is fairly a simple but high impact OPCODE)

I'd like to propose a discussion (and present an idea) around improving the stability of our testnets to provide a smoother experience for application developers.

In the spirit of my [post on Ethereum Magicians](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/methodology-for-ethereum-testnet-networks/23164), I'm suggesting the following for consideration and feedback:

- **Establish Hoodi as a long-standing testnet** dedicated to application development.
- **Exclude Hoodi from protocol fork testing**; instead, it should be forked from mainnet as closely as possible to avoid disruptions like those we’ve previously encountered.
- **Encourage developers to maintain a “staging” deployment** of their contracts on Hoodi, providing integrators and testers with a rich, stable environment.
- **Ensure that protocol forks are tested elsewhere first**, before being applied to Hoodi, to minimize potential issues as much as possible.

Could we discuss SFI'ing for next devnet

[EIP-7825](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7825): Transaction Gas Limit Cap

As it resolves an issues with increasing gaslimit (how does a user estimate gas on a tx that is too large in bytes, parallelization and fairness)

Also discuss the appropriate values for this EIP

e.g. for Tx Cap is ~5M~ ~10M~ 15M gas better than the 30M gas proposed 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d3c613f-867e-4025-aba3-77ac9e5f7535)

Considering all recent txs > 5M are decomposable (and 90% are XEN mining); a higher tx cap makes parallelizing harder; as if a block is a single tx consuming all gas it can only be run serially; as well as fairness for allowing other txs.

Could we discuss SFI'ing for next devnet

[EIP-7934](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7934): RLP Execution Block Size Limit

As it resolves the issue with block size breaking the network layer so preventing impossible to propagate blocks from being valid

Also discuss whether `10MiB - 512KiB` is the right size or if it needs to be more like `7.5MB` to allow for `2.5MiB` of slashings etc at the CL

Additionally whether this size is still too large for timely propagation on p2p given the upload recommendation of 50MBit/s; how many peers must it be sent to initially etc (10MiB being 80MBits)

Re Marc's point about a new platform for ACD.
I have created a pinned wiki topic on Eth Magicians as a portal for ACD info.  
https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/all-core-devs-acd/24198

We can experiment with the type of information we want to surface using the existing Eth Magicians platform.

Hello all,
I'd appreciate an opportunity to discuss our proposal to standardise JSON-RPC error codes across different execution clients
https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/658

Thank you @timbeiko. Appreciate it
This is mainly to let the client teams know this effort is underway & gather first round of feedback on the proposal before implementing it fully, as we have the framework ready to implement the solution.
The proposal PDF is attached to the [issue](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/658). 
Wanted to understand if the range of error codes defined in the proposal is good & the error groupings make sense for the users & clients alike, or a better grouping, if any.

Hey @timbeiko 
May I also present this EIP on the call? 😃  https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9792

> improve the `/pm` repo to be clearer

@timbeiko /pm repo needs an overhaul.

For each call we should have a file stored with:
* Agenda (copied from the Issue)
* Moderator summary of actions/decisions (copied from Eth Magicians, otherwise we change to having in the Issue)
* Raw transcript
* AI & (optionally) human improved transcript
* AI generated summary
* (Ideally) audio recording
* Raw chatlog
* Threaded chatlog (need to convert raw)
* Each calls files should be in a folder, matching the current call naming

Needs to be automated so we only need a human to review human improvements to transcripts.  
@nconsigny has been doing a great job on automation, so ideally this would be a continuation of that.

> [EIP-7934](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7934) : 10MB block limit enforced on block production
> ^^^^^^^^ - can we discuss why this limit should be in consensus, as opposed to an agreed operational limit?

It requires work to implement; and not specifying it as consensus means it is undefined behaviour.

Blocks larger than limit should be invalid; otherwise an EL receiving such a block (whether due to bug or otherwise) should try to run it and tell the CL to attest to it.

If they are valid it implies that the network is the part that should be fixed to allow larger than 10MiB blocks (80MBits); which then means the min recommended upload/download bandwidth should increase etc
